types: Five jobs: articulated rotates linked joints to position an assembly part; Cartesian/gantry slides on perpendicular axes to trace a print outline; SCARA uses planar rotary joints plus vertical travel to insert a component; delta uses three parallel linkages to transfer a lightweight part; mobile rover translates and turns to deliver a parcel. Different real robots can suit a job: accept a reasoned alternative while distinguishing the taught matching exercise. A robot body plan is its structure, not a brand or an animal phenotype. Ask learners to name one observed motion and connect it to the job.
anatomy: Base supports, rigid links connect rotating joints, motors drive joints, controller follows instructions, gripper is end effector. J1 base rotation, J2 shoulder, J3 elbow are three positioning axes. Opening/closing the gripper is separate, not a fourth positioning axis. The tool tilts with the links. Real sensors measure signals; Object held here is a calculated geometry result, not physical electronics. The assessment shows this teaching model with letter callouts: A base, B upper arm link, C shoulder joint, D motor/actuator, E gripper/end effector, F controller. Students answer one identification question at a time using A-F. The practical activity is a manual J1 turn using +10 or -10 degrees, not the old Joint controls toggle. Discuss the response and recorded evidence; do not invent what a label or learner action means.
coordinates: Joint angles are degrees, XYZ is TCP world position in millimetres from base. A joint rotation often changes multiple coordinates. For a straight vertical +10mm move, finalZ-initialZ=+10mm displacement, distance=10mm. Average speed=distance/simulated duration in seconds. Use supplied completed-move measurement only. Never invent duration or substitute demonstration values for learner measurements. Help use rational numbers and a one-variable equation; no trigonometry or Pythagoras assumed. The focused practice provides a Target Z field and Move button while X and Y remain fixed. Learners calculate starting Z plus 10, perform the real move, then Inspect joint changes. In Measure and explain, the start/finish height diagram and simulated duration are measured from that completed move. The calculation field in the snapshot is their latest submitted displacement, distance and speed. Check these against recentActions measurement; discuss mistakes with hints. A saved reflection follows checked calculations.
grip: Open, approach via fixture entrance, move to pickup, close, confirm Object held, lift10mm. Close does not prove successful grasp. TCP lies between jaws. Model uses alignment/contact geometry and virtual supports; no gravity/friction/force/impact dynamics. Invalid unsupported release is prevented. It is valid to reposition and retry.
program: Record ON saves successful moves and gripper changes. OFF allows exploration without adding steps. Reset returns robot/part to program start and retains steps. Run replays current program from matching state; Pause freezes it, Stop ends it. Build approach/pickup/close/lift/travel/lower/open/retreat. Judge recorded and replayed controller evidence, never mere clicks or target previews. Learner must test, identify a problem and improve.
obstacle: End position reachability is different from path clearance. Robot links, gripper and carried object can collide. Collision checking rejects unsafe moves before motion; it does not simulate impact. Slowing down does not fix geometric collision. Lift/cross/lower with verified clearance and intermediate positions; not every high route is safe. Independent destination B task requires learner route and test evidence. Do not give unverified safe coordinates.
design: Start with person and task. Explain chosen robot body plan, motion/job fit, benefit, limit and next investigation. Cite actual recorded program/obstacle tests if available. Simulated success is not real-world safety/performance proof. Multiple proposals may be valid. Help discover interests in making, coding, maths, design, science or helping people.
